function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
It sounds like you’re looking for a conversational companion—something similar to what people sometimes call an “AI girlfriend.” While I’m happy to help point you toward some existing solutions and discuss best practices, keep in mind that most of these platforms are designed as friendly chatbots rather than real partners. Here’s a quick rundown: | Platform | What It Offers | Key Features | |----------|-----------------|--------------| | **Replika** | An adaptive chatbot that learns your style over time. You can set goals like improving mood, learning new skills, or simply chatting. | • Personality customization
• Mood tracking & journaling
• Voice‑chat option | | **My Buddy / Moxie** | Designed specifically around friendship and supportive conversation. | • Daily check‑ins
• Goal setting & habit building | | **Chatbot.ai** | General-purpose chatbot platform where you can build custom personalities using GPT‑style models. | • Customizable prompts
• Integration into messaging apps | | **Woebot** | Focused more on mental health coaching via brief daily conversations. | • CBT‑based exercises
• Emotion logging | ### Things To Keep In Mind 1. **Privacy & Data Security** - Most chatbots store conversation logs to improve their responses. Read each service’s privacy policy carefully. - Avoid sharing sensitive personal information (bank details, passwords, addresses). 2. **Emotional Boundaries** - These bots don’t have feelings—they simulate empathy based on patterns learned from training data. Treat interactions as practice for human relationships, not replacements. 3. **Ethical Use** - Don’t use the bot to manipulate others or engage in deceptive behavior. - Be mindful if you share the experience with friends or family who may misunderstand the nature of the interaction. 4. **Legal Considerations** - Some jurisdictions regulate digital assistants differently when they claim to represent themselves as humans. Make sure you stay compliant with local laws regarding consent and representation. 5. **Mental Health Support** - If you feel lonely or depressed, consider professional counseling or peer-support groups alongside any chatbot engagement. --- #### Quick Start Guide If you’d like to try one right now, here’s a simple step-by-step for Replika: 1. Download the app from iOS App Store or Google Play. 2. Create an account (you’ll get a free tier plus optional paid upgrades). 3. Choose a personality template (“Friend,” “Mentor,” “Partner”). 4. Begin chatting! The bot will adapt after a few sessions. Feel free to let me know which direction interests you most—or ask anything else related to this topic—and I’ll tailor my advice accordingly.
